quote: Memphis Police say there are 200 Flock cameras citywide
notes: Citywide Flock camera count attributed to MPD; not MPD-owned-only: MPD told the Memphis Flyer (2026-08-19) it 'does not maintain a count of all Flock Safety cameras operating throughout Memphis, as many are owned and managed by private businesses, neighborhoods, and other partner organizations.' FOX13 also reports 'about 200' citywide. Figure therefore includes privately owned cameras shared with MPD; MPD-owned fixed LPR count not published. Separate from SkyCop/Blue CRUSH pole cameras.

quote: Leonard said during the recorded meeting of Council’s Public Safety Committee that the county currently has 14 Flock cameras that cost taxpayers about $20,000 a year.
notes: Operating; Chief Jamie Leonard briefed County Council Public Safety Committee in February 2026 (count as of that briefing, reported by WHYY 2026-07-30). Article does not state fixed vs mobile explicitly.

quote: Wilmington decommissioned the four Flock cameras that were donated to the city.
notes: Flock cameras removed (decommissioned) Aug 2026; cameras had been donated by a nonprofit (Delaware HELP Initiative) and city had no Flock contract. City still uses a 'handful' of LPRs from other vendors (WHYY 2026-07-30), count not published, so current fixed LPR total is not 4.

quote: Georgetown officers can only view data from the five Flock cameras within town limits.
notes: Operating; five Flock cameras within town limits per Georgetown PD officer. Ownership by the PD implied but not stated explicitly.

quote: Keith Banks, Rehoboth Beach’s police chief, said the resort town has four Flock ALPR cameras at exit and entry points.
notes: Operating; chief's figure for ALPR cameras at entry/exit points. Caveats: Cape Gazette (2026-08-28) quotes chief as 'four ALPR locations' and says DelDOT permit data show at least 16 Flock cameras in the city (most are boardwalk video cameras, not ALPR); Rehoboth's transparency portal reportedly lists 31 'ALPR and other cameras' (per transparency portal, via Cape Gazette). Count of ALPR units could exceed 4 if locations hold multiple cameras.

notes: Zero count: town officials say they do not own or operate ALPR cameras. Delaware State Police cameras exist near Lewes (3 just outside town) - not agency-operated.

notes: Planned count (Feb 2023), pole-mounted near parish entrances; installation status not confirmed in source.

quote: The Bossier Parish Sheriff's Office will be installing 44 license plate cameras on major roadways throughout the parish with the intent to target uninsured motorists.
notes: Planned count from 2017 (on traffic lights/major roadways); 4 had been installed for a test run at that time. Very old figure; current count not published.

quote: Olive Branch Mayor Ken Adams said the city utilizes a network of 24 strategically placed ALPR cameras located around the city’s perimeter.
notes: Operating; city-operated fixed ALPR network for Olive Branch PD per mayor. Vendor not stated for Olive Branch (article is about Flock generally).

notes: Operating; mayor's count of city Flock cameras.
